CANDIDATE_BINDING.rule: This record ratifies owner decisions AGAINST ONE EXACT EFFECTIVE PACKAGE, identified by the lane HEAD commit SHA and, independently, by the git blob SHA of each of the four M11 artifacts it comprises. Both must be re-derivable by inspection at any later time. If either check fails, the correct response is STOP_RATIFICATION_BINDING_MISMATCH - this record does not apply to a different candidate and must not be read as ratifying one.
CANDIDATE_BINDING.candidate_commit_verification: git rev-parse HEAD, on branch codex/cv1-m11-health-contract-adjudication-r1, at materialization.
CANDIDATE_BINDING.verification_method: git rev-parse <candidate_commit_sha>:<artifact path>, compared against expected_blob_sha1, for each of the four artifacts.
CANDIDATE_BINDING.on_mismatch: STOP_RATIFICATION_BINDING_MISMATCH. Any later amendment to any of the four artifacts (v1.0.4 or beyond) requires a SUCCESSOR ratification record binding to the new candidate; it does not retroactively apply to this one.

required_scope_of_the_separate_authority: STAGING-ONLY target - the principal must never be usable against, or confused with, a production identity.
MINIMUM PRIVILEGE - scoped to exactly what an authenticated M11 observation requires and no more.
CUSTODY - a named, accountable holder of the credential material.
ROTATION - a defined rotation cadence or trigger.
CREDENTIAL DELIVERY - a governed mechanism for how the credential reaches whatever runs the observation, without transiting insecure channels.
EVIDENCE - how the principal's creation, use, and state are evidenced for audit.
REVOCATION/EXPIRY - as appropriate to a staging test credential, so it does not become a standing, unmonitored access path.
owner_selected_decision.hard_constraint_preserved: The principal must NEVER be used as justification to lower or bypass the existing authentication boundary. This inherits MG-4 verbatim (v1.0.1 OD-5.constraint_inherited_not_reopened: 'the endpoints' auth requirement must NOT be relaxed to make measurement convenient. Lowering the boundary is not an option under OD-5'), and this ratification does not weaken, waive, or create an exception to it.

OD-1's A2 selection already makes M11 non-vacuous - by giving EP-1 a genuinely failable anonymous cell - before OD-5's principal exists. Authenticated EP-2/EP-3 coverage (Track B) is completed separately and later.

Does NOT specify who the principal is, what role it holds, or how it authenticates.
Does NOT open the separate authority lane itself - it authorizes that lane to be opened as a NEXT step.
Does NOT relax MG-4 or any existing authentication boundary in any respect.

CROSS_DECISION_COHERENCE.rule: These bindings are recorded explicitly so no reader has to re-derive how the five ratified decisions interact.

bindings.statement: OD-1's A2 selection makes M11 non-vacuous EVEN BEFORE OD-5's principal exists. Once implemented, an anonymous caller of /api/health/auth gets a genuinely failable cell (F-M11-13/M11-SC-8), which is the single thing the effective package's AF-M11-03 finding identified as missing.

OD-2's EP-2 = BLOCKING is the SELECTED FINAL contract, but its authenticated execution is CONTINGENT on OD-5's capability becoming real. Until then, the authenticated EP-2 cell is recorded as unavailable/pending, never as a silent pass. This is sequencing, not a weaker selection.

OD-3 is INDEPENDENT of OD-5 and contains NO principal authorization. The status-split decision can be implemented, tested, and deployed on its own schedule, entirely unblocked by whether or when OD-5's separate authority lane produces a principal.

OD-4's NOT_EXEMPT selection does NOT permit any future lane to treat the global rate limiter as a dependable abuse control. Its KV-conditional presence and fail-open failure mode (F-M11-20) mean OD-1's provider-health touch (option A2) must carry its own bounded budget regardless of what the shared limiter does or does not do in a given deployment - see OD-1's owner_approved_implementation_rider.

OD-5 authorizes ONLY the opening of a separate authority PROCESS for a durable staging principal - never the hosted act of creating, promoting, elevating, or using one. That act requires its own future authority, its own independent review, and its own owner confirmation, all downstream of this record.
